culture-description-aerial: Winged peoples of the high mountains. They keep more animals than harsh cultures, hunt from the air and avoid heavy armor and carts. Typical vocations: herder, farmer, hunter, weaver, mason, soldier.
culture-description-ascended: City-building craftsmen close to nature and more familiar with magic than other cultures, such as the elven nations. Any craft, often specialized; scholarly and magical vocations are common.
culture-description-coastal: Fishing villages on ocean shores or very large lakes: the rural counterpart of Mariner. Typical vocations: sailor, fisherman, chandler, sailmaker, rope maker.
culture-description-cosmopolitan: People of great cities, shaped by trade, highly specialized crafts and constant contact with foreigners and new ideas.
culture-description-dark: Powerful raider cultures that subjugate their neighbours, like Reavers but less literate (greater orcs and similar races). Typical vocations: raider, hunter, scout, bonesetter, shaman.
culture-description-fringe: The urban underclass that lives by night on the edge of the law and is distrusted by city folk. Typical vocations: gambler, bouncer, con artist, fence, thief.
culture-description-harsh: Peoples of hostile wastes (tundra, ice, lava, desert or blighted land) whose skills revolve around staying alive there.
culture-description-hermit: Private, self-sufficient households focused on knowledge that trade from home, as in gnome society. Typical vocations: scholar, librarian, researcher.
culture-description-highland: Isolated people of hills and mountains with little farmland, who combine small plots with herding.
culture-description-hunter: Hunters and gatherers of forests and jungles, like Sylvan but more martial and with fewer lores and crafts. Typical vocations: hunter, scout, farmer, weaver, leather worker.
culture-description-industrious: Hard-working societies that value crafting and trade, such as less martial dwarven nations. Usually several crafts. Typical vocations: miner, merchant, quartermaster, any craftsman.
culture-description-noble: Born into privilege: education, etiquette and the arts instead of a trade, mostly in cities. Typical vocations: knight, squire, courtier, adviser, landowner.
culture-description-nomad: Herders or hunters on the move with their animals. Mounts are central to their lives, and they value what can be carried over owning land.
culture-description-oceanic: Peoples who live mostly or only under the sea, like merfolk. Typical vocations: hunter, shaman, healer, seaweed and shellfish farmer.
culture-description-proud: Honour cultures quick to go to war, where battle earns status; either egalitarian or a warrior ruling class. Typical vocations: herder, farmer, soldier, militia, miner.
culture-description-reaver: Raider societies of the badlands near settled regions, living off the work of others with a little herding or farming.
culture-description-ritualist: Cold-blooded peoples with little food production, formal courtesy and elaborate social rituals. Typical vocations: seneschal, bodyguard, teacher, diplomat, priest, duellist.
culture-description-rural: Farmers and village craftsmen of open settled lands, who trade food and raw materials with nearby towns for manufactured goods.
culture-description-sanctified: A religious caste raised in a temple from birth to become clergy, well educated and free of trade. Typical vocations: priest, acolyte, musician, teacher, scribe.
culture-description-sea-raider: Reavers that operate from ships: warfare and survival at sea, few domestic animals. Typical vocations: captain, officer, rower, sailor, scout, shipbuilder.
culture-description-secret-nomad: Clans that travel and settle in hidden grottos, leaving no trace and keeping a close bond with the earth. Typical vocations: shaman, herder, craftsman, scout, hunter.
culture-description-singer: Peaceful wandering artists who prize music, crafts and foreign tongues and make their homes in remote places. Typical vocations: singer, musician, teacher, herder, merchant.
culture-description-skulker: Primitive raiders with little martial might that live subjugated or in hiding (goblins, kobolds, lesser orcs). Typical vocations: raider, hunter, scout, bonesetter, shaman.
culture-description-sylvan: Thinly spread forest dwellers who live mainly from hunting and gathering, with a little herding or farming.
culture-description-underground: Peoples living underground or in huge enclosed structures, fed by herds, fungus farms, fishing or trade.
culture-description-urban: Townsfolk of settled regions: specialists and craftsmen who swap finished goods for the food and materials of the countryside.

profession-description-adept: Essence alchemist and the classic item maker: enchants weapons, armour, potions, wands and almost any other object.
profession-description-assassin: Arms specialist in killing by stealth: ambushes, concealed weapons and poison rather than open battle.
profession-description-barbarian: Arms fighter from outside civilization who uses the wilderness, mobility and endurance, in lighter armor than a fighter.
profession-description-bard: Essence semi-spellcaster built around music and lore: a performer and collector of rumours whose songs confuse enemies, help allies and attune to magic items.
profession-description-cleric: Pure spellcaster of Channeling who draws straight on the power of a deity: life and healing, speaking with the gods, calling creatures and warding against rival faiths. Great power comes with strict obedience to the creed.
profession-description-dabbler: Essence semi-spellcaster who backs up stealth and trickery with magic, with a knack for deals and machines; in advanced settings, a natural engineer.
profession-description-druid: Pure spellcaster of the natural world: plants and herbs, beasts and weather. Can be played as a guardian of their people or as a rustic cultist.
profession-description-fighter: The combat specialist, from armoured knight to duellist or master archer. Whatever the weapons of the age, they train to stand at the centre of the fight.
profession-description-healer: Hybrid of Channeling and Mentalism who takes the wounds of others onto their own body and then recovers from them; a tough body and medical training come easily.
profession-description-illusionist: Pure spellcaster of Essence who fools the senses and the mind with false images, sounds and sensations. Indirect and subtle, yet as dangerous as a Magician.
profession-description-laborer: Trade and craft specialist. Handles weapons better than most casters and picks up athletics readily, but prefers work to fighting and focuses on the skills of a vocation.
profession-description-lay-healer: Pure spellcaster of Mentalism devoted to curing people and animals of wounds and disease, and to making and moving prostheses; mundane medicine is easy too.
profession-description-magent: Semi-spellcaster spy, half mage and half agent: poison, gathering secrets, discreet killing, escaping and shifting the blame onto someone else.
profession-description-magician: Pure spellcaster of the elements (earth, fire, ice, light, water and wind), whose bolts and balls make them a force on the battlefield; magical skills also come easily.
profession-description-mentalist: Pure spellcaster of Mentalism who works on minds and senses: detecting and contacting others, and dominating their will. Disciplines and social skills come naturally.
profession-description-monk: Semi-spellcaster who mixes Arms and Mentalism: personal spells fuel superhuman physical feats and stronger attacks.
profession-description-mystic: Hybrid of Essence and Mentalism with quiet magic: personal illusions and changing matter.
profession-description-no-profession: Balanced skill costs, used to build cultures or, optionally, in campaigns without professions where each character is defined only by the skills chosen. Broad but inefficient next to any real profession.
profession-description-outrider: Arms scout who rides ahead of the main force, tracking, watching for traps and moving unseen.
profession-description-paladin: Holy warrior and semi-spellcaster: a solid fighter and battlefield leader with supporting spells, at their best against the supernatural enemies of the faith.
profession-description-psychographer: Mentalism alchemist who fixes lasting psychic impressions in items, often drawing the powers from a living template.
profession-description-ranger: Semi-spellcaster of Arms and Channeling at home in the wild: tracking, moving unseen and surviving outdoors, helped by nature magic. A decent fighter and a dangerous raider.
profession-description-rogue: Jack of all trades among Arms users: a few weapons nearly as well as a Fighter, stealth and mechanisms nearly as well as a Thief, plus athletics and outdoor skills.
profession-description-sanctifier: Channeling alchemist who consecrates holy places, blesses tools of power and builds sanctuaries through the favour of a deity.
profession-description-scholar: Specialist in intellectual vocations. Trains weapons more easily than casters but usually lacks the physique; focuses on academic skills and learns spells better than other Arms users, short of true casters.
profession-description-sorcerer: Hybrid of Essence and Channeling devoted to destruction: of living beings (body, soul and mind) and of objects.
profession-description-swashbuckler: Arms fighter with style: well traveled and cultured, trained in every form of fighting and at ease socially.
profession-description-thief: Expert in stealth and subtlety. Locks, traps, climbing and deception come easily, and weapons reasonably so. Keeps to light armour; as useful as a scout or spy as a burglar.
profession-description-trader: Arms specialist in dealing with people: merchants, entertainers, diplomats and lay clergy.
profession-description-warrior-monk: Combat-focused relative of the Fighter who trusts discipline and agility rather than armour, like a ninja or a temple martial artist.
